rules.title: Santa Ana annual rent increase cap (Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance)
rules.requirement: For covered units, your landlord can raise rent only once a year, and by no more than 3% or 80% of the CPI change, whichever is lower. The cap is 2.87% for September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027. If your increase is higher, you can file a Tenant Petition with the Rent Stabilization Office.
rules.key_value: Lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change; 2.87% for 2026-09-01 to 2027-08-31
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance. This page does not list which units are covered.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.
rules.penalty: Tenants may petition for review of increases above the maximum allowable increase.

rules.title: Santa Ana just cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Your landlord needs a valid reason to evict you, such as unpaid rent, a lease violation, or the owner moving in. For some reasons, the landlord may also have to help pay your moving costs.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; relocation assistance for certain reasons
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance. This page does not list which units are covered.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.

notes: This is the City of Santa Ana's official page. It does not give a municipal code section number, an effective date for the ordinance, which units are covered, or any exemptions, so those fields are left empty. State law (Costa-Hawkins, Cal. Civ. Code § 1954.52) likely exempts newer buildings and single-family homes from the rent cap, but this page doesn't say so and I did not add those exemptions. The 2.87% figure is the published cap for Sept 1, 2026 to Aug 31, 2027. The page also mentions relocation assistance, but only vaguely; I put it in the just cause record rather than making a separate rule. I left out the $50-per-unit rental registry pass-through fee because it fits none of the six categories. Tenant petition procedures are also out of scope.
